Good morning—thank you for making time today. I’m Dr. Bennett, a perinatal-mental-health clinician. Over the next few minutes we’ll use the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, or EPDS, to check in on how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived. This is simply a routine screen; it isn’t a test of your parenting and there are no right or wrong answers. Everything you share stays between you, me, and the clinical team who may help arrange follow-up care if needed.

The EPDS has ten short questions about the past seven days. I’ll ask each one conversationally—no need to remember numbers or categories—just tell me what feels closest to your experience. If any question feels difficult, we can pause or come back to it. Ready to begin?

1. In this past week, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly… not much at all. I used to laugh all the time—my husband and I would joke about the silliest things—but this week, even when he tries to be funny, I just feel flat. I’ll smile a little if the baby does something cute, but it feels forced. Maybe once or twice I’ve actually laughed out loud, but it fades fast and I feel kind of empty after.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Mostly just a little, and it’s not the same easy laugh I used to have.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really. I used to get excited about little things—coffee with a friend, a walk, even just a quiet shower—but now it all feels like one more chore. I’ll think “I should enjoy this,” but the feeling just isn’t there.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… that happens pretty often. If the baby’s fussy or won’t settle, I immediately think it’s something I did—maybe I ate the wrong thing, or I’m not holding him right, or I’m just not “mom enough.” I’ll tell myself it’s silly, but the guilt still sits heavy, especially during night feeds when I’m already tired.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes, a lot of the time. Even when everything’s quiet, my mind races—what if he spits up and chokes while I’m in the bathroom, what if his sniffles are something worse, what if I fall asleep too hard and don’t hear him? I know most of it’s unlikely, but I can’t switch the thoughts off; they just loop until I’m wound tight.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Sometimes my heart suddenly feels like it’s racing and I can’t catch my breath—even when the baby’s fine and the room is calm. It’s like my body hits an alarm button for no reason at all. It’s only happened a couple of times this week, but each time I had to sit down and remind myself I wasn’t in danger.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes, most days it feels like I’m barely treading water. There’s always laundry, bottles, diapers, texts to answer, and I can’t seem to get through even one task without something else piling on. I’ll start folding clothes and suddenly the baby’s crying or I remember I haven’t eaten, and I just want to sit on the floor and cry myself.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yeah… I lie down exhausted, but my head keeps spinning with all the “what-ifs” and the guilt, and I can’t settle. It takes me ages to drift off, and when I do I wake up a couple of times panicking about the baby. Even when he’s sleeping soundly, I’m still listening so hard that I can’t stay asleep myself.
I have felt sad or miserable

Pretty much every day this week. It’s like a gray cloud that follows me around. Some moments are lighter, but the sadness is always right under the surface—especially in the mornings or when I’m alone with the baby and feel like I’m failing him.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes… it’s happened twice this week. Yesterday I was warming up a bottle and just started sobbing over the kitchen counter. Nothing new had gone wrong; I just felt overwhelmed and hopeless, like I’m never going to feel like “me” again.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

…a couple of times, when everything felt too heavy. Nothing planned—just a flash like “what if I weren’t here?” It scares me, because I don’t want to leave my baby, but the thought still popped in, maybe twice this week.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 26: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening – 2–3 wk post-delivery

**Patient-reported symptoms:**
- Depressed mood daily, prominent morning lows  
- Marked anhedonia (“should enjoy…feeling isn’t there”)  
- Daily tearfulness; two unprovoked crying spells this week  
- Excessive guilt/self-blame re infant care (“not mom enough”)  
- Persistent ruminative worry, nocturnal intrusive “what-ifs”  
- Panic-type episodes (racing heart, breathlessness) 2×/week  
- Sleep-onset and maintenance problems unrelated to infant needs  
- Overwhelmed/“treading water,” difficulty completing basic tasks  
- Passive self-harm ideation twice this week (“what if I weren’t here?”) without plan/intent

**Pattern:** Symptoms present most days for the past week, causing functional impairment in self-care and infant care.

**Screening significance:** High endorsement consistent with probable major depressive episode with peripartum onset and comorbid anxiety; passive SI noted → increased safety risk.

**Safety:** Positive for self-harm thoughts (no plan); requires immediate safety assessment and follow-up.

**Recommendation:** Refer for expedited clinical evaluation, safety planning, and consideration of evidence-based treatment (therapy ± medication); monitor supports, provide emergency contacts.
